elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim" — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", tracking the defined term in Section 1.2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall give Vendor prompt written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall control the defence of the claim" — control expressly allocated to Vendor.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Customer's indemnity obligations under this Agreement, if any, are limited to third-party claims arising out of Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law."

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted limb (a) covers third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims regarding the Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification exclusion was added, and none is required; the absence is Customer-favourable, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion inserted, which is more favourable to Customer than the fallback contemplates.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion inserted, so nothing to satisfy.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy; Section 9.3 still points to "the remedies required by Section 20.5", which does not exist in the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop tied to unavailability of procure/modify/replace appears anywhere in the inserted or retained language (Section 19.4's refund is a warranty remedy, not an IP-indemnity remedy).

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap was added; Section 21.3 continues to place "indemnification obligations" outside the liability cap.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the inserted paragraph delivers the defend-and-indemnify duty for Customer and its Affiliates, all four covered limbs (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the notice/control/cooperation mechanics, and an express cap on Customer's own indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

Fallback level is incomplete (procure/modify/replace, refund backstop and 3x super-cap all absent), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met and a super-cap would be a step down from Section 21.3, which currently leaves indemnification obligations uncapped.

Minimal: a single concise insertion in the vacant Section 20 slot after Section 19.5, no deletions or paraphrase of retained text, no survival tail, at-own-expense language, extra damages categories or other model-language extras beyond the selected elements; the drafter correctly refrained from importing fallback-only remedies and a super-cap.

Preserves intent: Sections 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3 and 30.5 all presuppose an indemnity and now have an operative referent; nothing retained contradicts the new clause and the Excluded Claims carve-out for indemnification obligations continues to operate.

Repair note (not a failure of the checklist): Section 9.3's cross-reference to "Section 20.5" remains dangling because the pre-existing Section 20 is absent and the inserted text supplies no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy. Either renumber/insert those remedies as Section 20.5 or conform Section 9.3's cross-reference to the new indemnity section so the termination trigger is not inoperable.

Drafting check: confirm the inserted paragraph carries its section number (rendered text appears unnumbered) and that "Affiliates", "Customer Data" and "Deliverables" are defined in Section 1; if any is undefined, add the definition to avoid an undefined capitalised term.
